title: Two reading cards: recorded is exact, an estimate has a badge
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as a service advisor with the view customers and create and edit customers permissions.
  2. Seed a test unit (e.g. unit 402)'s reading history by hand (standard steps; Mark complete on a work order records that work order's mileage and engine hours as readings dated its Reset date):
  3. ↳ In Settings > Maintenance (needs Settings Service) create, once, a throwaway schedule "ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed" with one routine service per reading: "ZZ Seed 1", "ZZ Seed 2" (calendar Every 12 months each). Enrol the unit on it (its Maintenance tab > Enroll in Schedule, dates blank).
  4. ↳ For each reading below, oldest first: Work Orders > New Work Order for the unit; type the mileage (and the engine hours, where given) in the work order's Mileage (and Engine Hours) field; on that work order's maintenance card open the next "ZZ Seed" service's row menu > Mark complete > On a work order (this work order) > Reset date = the date given > Mark complete. A Reset date is never in the future.
  5. ↳ Readings: ZZ Seed 1: Reset date 120 days before today, Mileage 100,000; ZZ Seed 2: Reset date 60 days before today, Mileage 104,000.
  6. ↳ Then remove the unit from the throwaway schedule (Maintenance tab > schedule menu > Remove from schedule), and enrol it on any schedule with a mileage-driven service (e.g. "Highway Tractor PM" with PM-A: calendar Every 12 months + Distance Every 15,000 mileage), dates blank, so its Maintenance tab shows the reading cards. A unit whose past invoiced work orders already carry the same history may be used instead.
  7. If Mark complete does not record a seeded reading (the Mileage or Engine Hours card does not show that value and date afterwards), stop: mark this case Blocked and write "seeding failed: Mark complete did not record the reading" in the result comment. That is a separate problem with its own case, not a failure of this one.
custom_steps:
1. On the Maintenance tab read the two reading cards (mileage on the left, engine hours on the right).
  2. On the recorded card check for any qualifier next to the value; on the estimated card read the badge and the line explaining its basis.
  3. Find a Low confidence meter and read its colour.
  4. Hover the (i) beside the mileage "Current estimate".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The tab opens with the two reading cards: mileage says it is recorded (104,000, recorded 60 days ago) and shows an estimate beside it; engine hours has no reading yet.
  • The recorded 104,000 shows exactly, with no qualifier; the estimate carries a badge (e.g. "Estimated") and its basis (e.g. "measured from 2 visits").
  • The mileage confidence reads Low (one usable pair, last reading 60 days old) and its meter is not red.
  • On the design the (i) reads "The estimate works out a rate from the last three usable pairs of readings, read as one period, and carries the last reading forward at that rate. At least two readings are needed for any estimate. A new recorded reading replaces it outright."

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10566 (S9, The asset Maintenance tab), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S9 (The two reading cards; S9-R1, S9-R2, S9-R17; S11-R24 copied from Chunk 2); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard S4; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R1: “The tab will open with current readings: distance and engine hours, each showing whether it is recorded or estimated, with its age”
  • S9-R2: “A recorded reading will show the exact value with no qualifier. An estimate will carry a badge and its basis”
  • S11-R24: “31 to 90 days: one pair Low”
  • S9-R17: “The confidence meter's Low state is never red. Red is reserved for overdue”
  • Design board, artboard S4 (estimate (i)): “The estimate works out a rate from the last three usable pairs of readings, read as one period, and carries the last reading forward at that rate. At least two readings are needed for any estimate. A new recorded reading replaces it outright.”
